name: Carcinoma of Esophagus, Salivary Gland Type
aliases: Salivary Gland-Type Adenocarcinoma of the Esophagus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Esophageal Salivary Gland-Type Carcinoma

criteria.description: Presence of salivary gland-type carcinoma histological features (e.g., adenoid cystic or mucoepidermoid patterns) in esophageal biopsy or resection specimen
Immunohistochemical staining positive for salivary gland markers such as cytokeratin 7 (CK7), S100, and myoepithelial markers
Exclusion of primary salivary gland carcinoma with esophageal metastasis by clinical and radiological evaluation
Imaging confirming primary tumor localized to the esophagus without distant primary source

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of salivary gland-type carcinoma in esophageal tissue with supportive immunohistochemical profile and exclusion of primary salivary gland tumor
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including pathology, radiology, and clinical correlation.

searchTerms: mass seen in esophagus during endoscopy

common.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice due to nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Cough due to tracheoesophageal fistula formation
Hoarseness without nerve involvement (due to local inflammation)

rare.symptomName: Distant metastasis presenting as bone pain
searchTerms: pain due to distant tumor metastasis

laboratory: Mild anemia due to chronic disease
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in advanced cases
imaging: Esophageal mass on barium swallow or esophagram
Mass lesion on CT scan localized to esophagus
genetic: No well-established genetic mutations specific to this carcinoma subtype
other: Histopathology showing salivary gland-type carcinoma features
Immunohistochemical positivity for CK7, S100, and myoepithelial markers

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows squamous differentiation rather than salivary gland-type features
More common in smokers and alcohol users
Primary tumor located in salivary glands with secondary esophageal involvement
Clinical and radiological evidence of salivary gland primary
Arises from Barrett’s esophagus or glandular epithelium
Histology shows glandular differentiation without salivary gland features

redFlags: New onset hoarseness or voice changes
Signs of airway obstruction or fistula formation
